title: Signed double-Hom comparison with a mapping cone
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Work with integer-indexed cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix any such complex $I$ and put $T(C)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(C,I)$, with differential and contravariant action on chain maps as in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Use $C[m]^n=C^{n+m}$, $d_{C[m]}=(-1)^m d_C$, and the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $\operatorname{Cone}(u)^n=B^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ for $u:A\to B$, with differential $(b,a)\mapsto(d_Bb+u(a),-d_Aa)$, inclusion $i:B\to\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, and projection $\pi:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to A[1]$.

There are natural chain isomorphisms $s_{C,m}:T(C[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}T(C)[-m]$ whose value on a homogeneous map of degree $q$ is $(-1)^{mq}$ times the same map with its source components reindexed. Put
$$\chi_C=-s_{T(C),-1}\circ T(s_{C,1})^{-1}:T^2(C[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}T^2(C)[1].$$
For $g\in T^2(C[1])^p$ and $y\in T(C)^r$, this is $(\chi_Cg)(y)=(-1)^{p+r}g(y)$, where on the right $y$ is read in $T(C[1])^{r+1}$ by reindexing without an additional sign.

For every chain map $u:A\to B$, set $E=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, $X=T(B)$ and $Y=T(A)$. Under the graded decomposition $T(E)^q=X^q\oplus Y^{q-1}$, write a degree-$p$ local section of $T^2(E)$ as $(\alpha,\beta)$, with $\alpha_q:X^q\to I^{q+p}$ and $\beta_r:Y^r\to I^{r+p+1}$. The formula
$$\theta_u(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha,\gamma),\qquad \gamma_r=(-1)^{p+r}\beta_r$$
defines a chain isomorphism $\theta_u:T^2(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(T^2u)$, natural in commutative squares of chain maps. It satisfies
$$\theta_u\circ T^2(i)=i_{T^2u},\qquad \chi_A\circ T^2(-\pi)=-\pi_{T^2u}\circ\theta_u.$$
No boundedness, flatness or K-injectivity is assumed on $A,B,I$.

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon(t)=(-1)^t$ for integers $t$. All formulas below are morphisms of restricted module sheaves over each object $U$ and commute with further restriction. For $f\in T(C[m])^q$, reindexing makes $f$ a map of degree $q-m$ from $C$ to $I$. The Hom differential [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $d f=d_I f-\epsilon(q+m)f d_C$. Set $s_{C,m}(f)=\epsilon(mq)f$. Both $s_{C,m}(df)$ and $d_{T(C)[-m]}s_{C,m}(f)$ are
$$\epsilon(mq+m)d_I f-\epsilon(mq+q)f d_C.$$
Thus $s_{C,m}$ is a chain map. Its inverse multiplies a reindexed degree-$q$ element by the same sign. For a chain map $a:C\to C'$, precomposition with $a[m]$ before reindexing and with $a$ afterwards produces the identical family $\epsilon(mq)f a$; this proves naturality.

proof.text:
For $g\in T^2(C[1])^p$ and $y\in T(C)^r$, view $y$ without sign in $T(C)[-1]^{r+1}$ and in $T(C[1])^{r+1}$. The inverse of $s_{C,1}$ sends the first copy to $\epsilon(r+1)y$. Since $T$ acts by precomposition [def-pur-hom-complex], $T(s_{C,1})^{-1}(g)$ evaluated there equals $\epsilon(r+1)g(y)$. Step 1 applied to the complex $T(C)$ and $m=-1$ multiplies a degree-$p$ element by $\epsilon(p)$. Including the defining leading minus sign gives
$$ (\chi_Cg)(y)=-\epsilon(p)\epsilon(r+1)g(y)=\epsilon(p+r)g(y). $$
This also verifies the domains of the composite: $T(s_{C,1})^{-1}$ lands in $T(T(C)[-1])$, and $s_{T(C),-1}$ lands in $T^2(C)[1]$. It is a natural chain isomorphism as a composite of the natural chain isomorphisms of step 1 and their images under $T$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula; derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone). Explicit agent calculation filling the omission in Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text:
Put $v=T(u):X\to Y$. By the cone definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], a degree-$q$ map $E\to I$ is uniquely a pair $(x,y)$ with $x\in X^q$ and $y\in Y^{q-1}$: its component sends $(b,a)$ to $x(b)+y(a)$. The inverse decomposition takes restrictions to the two summands. This assertion uses no interchange of infinite sums and products: a map from each binary direct sum is determined by two restrictions, and the inverse family is given by addition in each degree. Substituting $d_E(b,a)=(d_Bb+u(a),-d_Aa)$ in the Hom differential gives
$$ d_{T(E)}(x,y)=(d_Xx,\ d_Yy+\epsilon(q+1)v(x)). $$
Indeed, the second component is $d_Iy+\epsilon(q)y d_A-\epsilon(q)x u$, while the first is $d_Ix-\epsilon(q)x d_B$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula; derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone). Explicit agent calculation filling the omission in Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text:
Apply the same binary-summand decomposition to $\operatorname{Hom}(T(E)^q,I^{q+p})$. A degree-$p$ element has the unique components $(\alpha,\beta)$ in the statement, with $g(x,y)=\alpha_q(x)+\beta_{q-1}(y)$. Denote its differential by $(\alpha',\beta')$. Evaluate $d_Ig-\epsilon(p)g d_{T(E)}$ using step 3, first on $(x,0)$ in degree $q$ and then on $(0,y)$ in degree $r+1$. It gives
$$\alpha'_q=d_I\alpha_q-\epsilon(p)\alpha_{q+1}d_X^q+\epsilon(p+q)\beta_qv^q,$$
$$\beta'_r=d_I\beta_r-\epsilon(p)\beta_{r+1}d_Y^r.$$
Here $\alpha$ has degree $p$ as a map $X\to I$, while the reindexed $\beta$ has degree $p+1$ as a map $Y\to I$. These formulas are direct expansions of [def-pur-hom-complex]; they do not assume exactness of an infinite product.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula; derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone). Explicit agent calculation filling the omission in Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text:
Set $\gamma_r=\epsilon(p+r)\beta_r$. Since $T^2u=T(v)$ is precomposition with $v$ [def-pur-hom-complex], step 4 gives $\alpha'=d_{T(X)}\alpha+(T(v)\gamma)$. For the second component of $\theta_u(dg)$ the same step gives
$$\epsilon(p+1+r)\beta'_r=\epsilon(p+r+1)d_I\beta_r+\epsilon(r)\beta_{r+1}d_Y^r=-\bigl(d_{T(Y)}\gamma\bigr)_r.$$
Thus $\theta_u(dg)=(d_{T(X)}\alpha+T(v)\gamma,-d_{T(Y)}\gamma)$, exactly the differential in $\operatorname{Cone}(T^2u)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its inverse in degree $p$ is $(\alpha,\gamma)\mapsto(\alpha,\beta)$ with $\beta_r=\epsilon(p+r)\gamma_r$. The two composites are identity maps since $\epsilon(p+r)^2=1$. Consequently $\theta_u$ is a chain isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula; derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone). Explicit agent calculation filling the omission in Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text: For a commutative square $b u=u'a$ with $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$, the cone map $h:E\to E'$ is $h(b_0,a_0)=(b(b_0),a(a_0))$. Substituting the cone differentials shows $d_{E'}h=h d_E$, using exactly $bu=u'a$ and the chain-map equations for $a,b$. By precomposition [def-pur-hom-complex], $T(h)$ sends $(x',y')$ to $(T(b)x',T(a)y')$. Hence $T^2(h)$ sends $(\alpha,\beta)$ to $(\alpha\circ T(b),\beta\circ T(a))$ componentwise. The second component after applying $\theta_{u'}$ is $\epsilon(p+r)\beta_r\circ T(a)^r$, which equals the second component after applying $\theta_u$ followed by the cone map $(T^2b,T^2a[1])$; their first components also agree. This proves the asserted naturality. The cone map on the target is a chain map by the same displayed cone calculation, since $T^2$ preserves the square by twice precomposing.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula; derived.tex Tag 014E (definition-cone). Explicit agent calculation filling the omission in Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated).

proof.text:
The map $T(i):T(E)\to X$ is $(x,y)\mapsto x$ by precomposition [def-pur-hom-complex], so $T^2(i)$ sends $\alpha$ to $(\alpha,0)$ and $\theta_uT^2(i)$ is the cone inclusion. Next $T(-\pi):T(A[1])\to T(E)$ sends a degree-$q$ element $z$ to $(0,-z)$, with $z$ reindexed as an element of $Y^{q-1}$. Thus $T^2(-\pi)(\alpha,\beta)$ evaluated on $z$ is $-\beta_{q-1}(z)$. For $y\in Y^r$, step 2 now gives
$$\bigl(\chi_A T^2(-\pi)(\alpha,\beta)\bigr)(y)=-\epsilon(p+r)\beta_r(y)=-\gamma_r(y).$$
This is precisely $-\pi_{T^2u}\theta_u(\alpha,\beta)$ by the cone projection of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equality on all restricted sheaf maps proves the two arrow equations. All constructions used binary summands, reindexing, and multiplication by signs, so there is no boundedness, flatness, or K-injectivity requirement.
